about: The project's task cards under the tailored R&D life-cycle gates (NASL-EMS-HBK-001 and the project plan NASL-SHD-PMP-001). The project is done when every card is done and every gate is passed. Each card: id, gate, title, lead, support, status (todo, in progress, needs you, done), priority (now, next, later, done), purpose, entry {gate, criteria}, exit {gate, criteria}, predecessors, successors (derived from the predecessors), inputs, outputs, verification, size (the scope: S one engineer and one pass, M two or three engineers or two passes, L several engineers and system runs, XL every subsystem or several safety chains), effort (in engineering passes, when done), risks {risk, likelihood, impact, mitigation}, escalation {when, to}, decisions (the user's open decision numbers), links, report, task, note. Gate status: open, passed. Edit this file to add or update cards; the dashboard's Project tab shows it, and tools/reports/build_task_cards.py makes the PDF.

Each software owner generates the C from the saved models, traces every block to its C function and lines, and lists each function with its tests and requirements. The test engineer runs every test class with the scenario reruns on, every scenario but S3. The integration engineer describes the system's states and modes and how the state machines work together, and the data analyst shows from the runs which transitions each scenario exercised. The card delivers the software design description NASL-SHD-SDD-002, generated from the model and the code, and the engineering report NASL-SHD-ER-007.
